review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for `-Periodic`/`-Antiperiodic` simp-set uses. I did not run Lean, so I did not check how many downstream proofs depend on the `@[simp]` unfolding, and I did not check whether removing it would break any. The two findings are one pattern: `@[simp]` on a predicate `def`. I found no rewrite loops or conflicting lemmas, and I did not recommend simp attributes on the conditional `Periodic.*_eq` lemmas.

findings.problem: `@[simp]` on a predicate `def` makes every `simp` or `simp_all` call anywhere unfold `Periodic f c` to `∀ x, f (x + c) = f x`. Unfolding hides the named predicate, so hypotheses `h : Periodic f c` stop matching lemmas stated with `Periodic`. The file itself works around this: `Finset.periodic_prod` has to write `simpa [-Periodic]` to switch the unfolding off, and `Periodic.neg` has to list `Periodic` explicitly, which would be redundant if the attribute were consistently relied on. In-file proofs such as `Periodic.comp`, `.mul`, `.div`, `.smul` and `add_period` use bare `simp_all`, so they silently depend on this global unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `simp` from the attribute, leaving `@[wikidata Q184743]`. Make the dependent proofs name the unfolding explicitly, e.g. `by simp_all [Periodic]` in `Periodic.comp`, `.mul`, `.div`, `.smul`, `.add_period` and `Periodic.nsmul`. Then drop the `-Periodic` in `Finset.periodic_prod`. Where it is needed, `unfold_let`-free `intro x` followed by `simp [h x]` would also work. Downstream files that depend on the unfolding would need `simp [Function.Periodic]`.
findings.benefit: The simp set no longer eagerly expands a named predicate. Hypotheses and goals of the form `Periodic f c` stay intact for lemmas such as `Periodic.add_period` and `Periodic.nsmul`. The `simpa [-Periodic]` workaround disappears, and each proof shows where it unfolds the definition.

findings.problem: This has the same problem as `Periodic`: `@[simp]` on a predicate `def` makes simp unfold `Antiperiodic f c` into a `∀` statement everywhere. Several in-file proofs (`Antiperiodic.periodic`, `.smul`, `.mul`, `.div`, `.add`, `Periodic.add_antiperiod`) call bare `simp_all`, and that only works because of the global unfolding. `Antiperiodic.neg` also passes `Antiperiodic` to `simpa only` explicitly.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `Antiperiodic`. Write the unfolding explicitly in the proofs that need it, e.g. `simp_all [Antiperiodic]` or `simp_all [Periodic, Antiperiodic, neg_div_neg_eq]`. Do the same for `Periodic` so the two predicates behave consistently.
findings.benefit: This keeps `Antiperiodic` and `Periodic` as opaque named predicates in the default simp set. Lemmas whose statements mention them stay applicable after simp. The reader can also see which proofs depend on unfolding the definitions.
